672  Part 4 Nutrition Therapy
Clinical Manifestations
Th e signs and symptoms associated with an upper respiratory 
infection are usually mild and brief in duration. Th ese include 
the cardinal symptoms of inﬂ ammation (rubor, calor, dolor, 
and functio laesa; see Chapter 9). Fluid and mucus released in 
response to the inﬂ ammation obstruct upper airways. If the
inﬂ ammation includes the larynx, trachea, and upper bronchi, 
the patient will experience labored breathing. Th ese symptoms 
may be more diﬃ  cult for infants and children due to their im-
mature respiratory system and accessory muscles of the neck.
